conviction_note: The 2Q26 release (13 Jul) guided 3Q and 4Q on all-in fuel of $3.20 and $3.00 a gallon. Delta then realised $3.61 against its own $3.15 assumption and guides 4Q at $4.25, and Aeromexico's CEO warned twice that fuel is above plan. So a 3Q margin shortfall and a cut to the FY guide are close to certain. But the warnings, Delta's cut and a stock still 28% below its high mean much of this is known, and AERO is up about 6% since Delta's print. Findings sum to -1.5. The scaled number is p_up 42 on a 5.5% absolute move, i.e. -0.88: smaller than the sum because the negative is a widely telegraphed industry fact and Citi argues Aeromexico can pass fuel through.
bar: Company guide from the 2Q26 release, 6-K of 2026-07-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001561861/000119312526302103/d112634dex991.htm). 3Q26: ASMs +0.5% to +1.5%, revenue $1.59-1.62bn (+12-14%), adj. EBITDAR margin 26.5-29.5%, operating margin 14-17%, fuel ~$3.2/gal all-in, FX 17.5 MXN/USD. 4Q26: revenue $1.64-1.68bn, EBITDAR 28-31%, operating margin 15.5-18.5%, fuel ~$3.0/gal. FY26: revenue +13-14%, EBITDAR 24-26%, operating margin 11-13%. Street EPS is not usable as a bar: sources range from $0.24 to $0.61 (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/aero, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AERO/earnings-forecasts, https://tickflow.io/stock/AERO/forecast). print_vs_bar_pct is revenue against the $1.605bn guide midpoint: 3Q RPMs ran about +3% y/y in Aug and Sep against ASM guidance of +0.5-1.5%.
positioning_check: Short interest is light: 699.7k ADS on the 2026-07-31 settlement, 3.2 days to cover (https://stockmarketwatch.com/stock/AERO), about 0.7% of float per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AERO/sentiment). No newer settlement was found, and this is not a crowded short. The baseline option chain is unusable (ATM spread 153% of mid, total OI 200, put/call OI 0.05), so there is no skew or implied move. Tape: spot $16.505, 20d +3.48%, 5d +2.71%, 28% below the 52w high, below the $19 IPO price. Sell-side 12m targets are stale at about $27-28 (MarketBeat, 11 analysts).

findings.finding: 3Q26 fuel ran well above the $3.20/gal all-in assumption in the guide. Delta's 3Q (reported 2026-10-09) realised $3.61 against a $3.15 July assumption, +46c or about +15%, and absorbed more than $500m of fuel above guidance. On about 118m gallons (2Q used 444.7m litres = ~117.5m gal), the same overrun costs Aeromexico roughly $50-70m, or 3-4.5 points of margin on $1.6bn of revenue. That puts the 14-17% operating-margin and 26.5-29.5% EBITDAR guide at risk unless pricing recaptures more than 2Q's ~75%. The overrun in 2Q was only $30m, and 2Q still landed in line with guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last confirmed print, 2Q26 (2026-07-13 amc): results in line with guide despite a $30m fuel overrun and a net loss; the baseline records +2.29% for that session. The 1Q26 print (2026-04-21 amc) is not in the baseline history, whose other rows are monthly traffic reports, so there is no clean earnings base rate.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the CEO warned in the Aug and Sep traffic releases that fuel is 'higher than previously anticipated'. But no quantified Aeromexico number exists, the EPS estimates are scattered from $0.24 to $0.61, and targets sit at $27-28, so the size of the margin shortfall has not been set. If the market had fully priced a 3-4 point margin miss, the stock would not have risen about 6% since Delta's 10-09 print.
findings.independence: Same direction from the company's own wording, in two separate releases: Sep traffic, 2026-10-06 (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results), and Aug traffic, 2026-09-03 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2664877196). Guide assumption from the 2Q26 6-K. Shares the Delta document with the guidance finding below, but lands on a different line (the reported quarter vs the forward guide).

findings.finding: The 4Q26 and FY26 guide is built on $3.00/gal fuel, while Delta's 4Q guide (2026-10-09) assumes about $4.25. A gap of $1.00-1.25/gal on about 120m gallons is $120-150m, or 7-9 points of 4Q margin before recapture. So the 15.5-18.5% 4Q operating-margin guide and the 11-13% FY guide are very likely cut, or recast with a fare and capacity response. Precedent: Delta cut FY EPS by 24% at the midpoint and traded about -2.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No confirmed Aeromexico guidance cut since the Nov-2025 IPO. Peer precedent: Delta -2.9% on a 24% FY EPS cut whose midpoint ($5.35) was already near the $5.46 consensus (https://finviz.com/news/400853/delta-air-lines-shares-fall-as-third-quarter-earnings-miss-forecasts-and-full-year-outlook-is-cut).
findings.why_not_priced: The stale $3.00 assumption sits in the company's own 6-K and has not been withdrawn. Aggregator targets ($27-28) and the spread in estimates suggest many models still carry the July guide. Had a 7-9 point 4Q margin reset been priced, AERO would not have rallied after Delta cut. The opposite case is also live: the cut is so widely expected that 'less bad' fare recapture could be bought.
findings.independence: Delta's 4Q fuel assumption of $4.25 (https://beancount.io/blog/2026/10/10/delta-air-lines-q3-2026-earnings-analysis). The Aeromexico CEO's 2026-10-06 wording on fuel 'more challenging than anticipated' (https://finviz.com/news/399318/aeromexico-september-2026-traffic-results). Also, at the 2Q call (July) the company said it would cut 4Q capacity if fuel volatility persisted (https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2026/07/27/las-aerolineas-mexicanas-pierden-mas-de-3-mil-300-millones-de-pesos-por-el-fuerte-aumento-en-el-precio-de-la-turbosina-durante-el-segundo-trimestre-de-2026/).

findings.finding: The pilots' contract is unresolved. On 2026-09-30, ASPA rejected Aeromexico's offer (reported as a 3.2% raise) and requested an extension of up to 45 days, which runs to around mid-November. The call on 10-20 will be asked about the labour cost embedded in any revised guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in this listing. The 2024 pilot deal (7.5% wage raise) settled without a strike.
findings.why_not_priced: Spanish-language press only; it does not appear in English wire coverage of AERO, and the strike deadline itself falls after the window. Only the call commentary and any CASM-ex-fuel guide change land inside the window.
findings.independence: Earlier strike notice with a 09-30 deadline (https://elceo.com/negocios/aeromexico-entra-en-turbulencia-pilotos-ponen-fecha-limite-para-evitar-una-huelga/, 2026-09-02). Rejected 3.2% offer (https://aerocorner.com/news/aeromexico-pilots-strike-deadline-october-1/).

findings.finding: 3Q traffic ran ahead of the capacity guide. Total RPMs were +2.9% y/y in August and +3.6% in September, against 3Q ASM guidance of +0.5% to +1.5%. Load factor was 89.7% in Aug (+0.6pp) and 87.1% in Sep (+0.1pp), and international RPMs grew +4.3% and +6.6%. Together with management's 'forward bookings healthy' wording, this points to revenue at or slightly above the $1.59-1.62bn guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26 printed a record revenue of $1.479bn, in line with guidance, and the stock rose +2.29% that session. Monthly traffic days in the baseline move -4.7% to +4.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the traffic releases are public. Yield (TRASM) is not in them, so the size of any revenue beat from fare recapture is the unpublished part.
findings.independence: August traffic release, 2026-09-03 (https://www.itiger.com/news/2664877196). Delta reported record revenue +16% and said demand was strong (https://finviz.com/news/400853/delta-air-lines-shares-fall-as-third-quarter-earnings-miss-forecasts-and-full-year-outlook-is-cut).

findings.finding: Citi (as reported 2026-10-12) says Aeromexico is better placed than Volaris to pass high fuel through to fares, citing premium mix, long-haul international and its AICM hub, and expects no material demand damage. It also flags that AICM's move to 48 operations an hour at the end of October could restore slots. Citi calls a Volaris guidance revision 'probable' but makes no such call on Aeromexico.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a sell-side view and probably part of why AERO rose after Delta's cut, so it is largely in the price. It is filed because the call can confirm or deny the fare pass-through and the AICM slot gain.
findings.independence: 2Q fuel recapture of about 75-76% is in the company's own release and call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/grupo-aeromexico-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-14/). It is shown as a summary only and could not be fetched.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-20 the Eleventh Circuit vacated DOT's September 2025 order ending antitrust immunity for the Delta-Aeromexico JV, so coordinated pricing, scheduling and revenue sharing stay in place. This removes a 2026 overhang that the guide may not have assumed away.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on an earnings day. The ruling came out between prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: public for two months. Only commentary on the call about JV economics or a DOT rehearing request lands in the window.

findings.finding: Domestic competition is mixed. Volaris grew 3Q ASMs +11.1% (domestic +11.0%) against Aeromexico domestic ASMs of -3.4% in September. But Volaris cut September capacity 22% from its summer peak, and Citi expects Volaris to revise its guidance. Pressure on domestic yield and capacity relief roughly offset.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a competitor proxy, not an Aeromexico number. Domestic is about a quarter of Aeromexico's ASMs, so it is sized net of the international business, which is growing.

outside_window.finding: ASPA strike extension of up to 45 days from 2026-10-01 expires around mid-November. A strike or a costly settlement would resolve then, not inside this window.

rejected_candidates.detail: Most of these rows are monthly traffic 6-Ks, not prints. The sweep row and the 1Q26 release dated 2026-04-21 (not in the history) contradict their use as an earnings base rate. Only 2026-07-13 (+2.29%) is a confirmed print.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The negative lean cuts against the 20d run-up of +3.5% and the roughly 6% rally since Delta's cut, which suggests the market already expects a fuel reset and may reward a credible fare-recapture story, so p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 / 'inside what was guided': the 3Q fuel overrun was pre-warned twice by the CEO, so that finding went from -1.0 to -0.8
Rule 1 and the pessimism artefact: the guidance cut is an industry-wide, telegraphed fact (Delta, and AERO's rally since), so that finding went from -1.5 to -1.2 and p_up from 40 to 42

Untrustworthy-history lesson: rebuilt from confirmed releases (only 2Q26 at +2.29% is in the baseline), so abs_move_pct is set on airline guidance-reset scale (5.5) rather than the 3.16% traffic-day median
Rule 7: checked short interest (about 0.7% of float, DTC 3.2), not crowded, so no squeeze haircut was needed
Rules 4, 5 and 9 left the other findings standing: the competitor proxy (Volaris) was sized net of international and kept at 0
